3. **Weight Calculation:** Compute the interpolation weight $w$ within the interval $[points[i].position, points[i+1].position]$ [S1, S4, unofficial]:

The claim describes the calculation of an interpolation weight $w$ within an interval defined by control point positions. Source [S1] explicitly defines this weight as $w = (t - points[i].pos) / range$, where $range = points[i+1].pos - points[i].pos$. Source [S4] describes a similar process using variables $A$ and $B$ for the interval boundaries and $P$ for the sampled value, calculating the weight as $a / (a + b)$ where $a = P - A$ and $b = B - P$. Since $a + b = (P - A) + (B - P) = B - A$, the formula in [S4] is mathematically equivalent to the one in [S1]. Both sources support the fact that the weight is computed based on the position of the sample relative to the interval boundaries.
